title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff/regional failover ordering
author: Avery Chen
release_notes: Fixes race in SLO enforcer backoff ordering that could cause regional failovers to trigger prematurely under bursty load. Deployed hotfix to stabilize failover ordering and reduce unnecessary cross-region traffic.
description:
Context and motivation: During a recent incident (SUP-4321) we observed the SLO enforcer's backoff/backpressure ordering race under bursty multi-region traffic. The enforcer would in some cases mark a region as degraded and trigger failover while a subsequent backoff reconciliation loop re-enabled the region, leading to oscillation and excess cross-region replication load. This PR contains a targeted hotfix that fixes ordering and adds additional guards to avoid premature regional failovers.

Summary of changes (single-line commits overview):
- Fix ordering: ensure backoff state transitions are applied atomically and reconciled with latest region health snapshot.
- Add a short jittered cooldown window before initiating regional failover when backoff is detected concurrently.
- Tighten metrics and tracing around SLO enforcer decision points for post-mortem analysis.
- Add unit and integration tests that simulate concurrent backoff/reconcile races and confirm stable outcome.

Changed areas/files (high-level):
- internal/slo/enforcer.go: reorder state machine transitions, add atomic compare-and-set for region status (small patch, ~80 LOC).
- internal/slo/reconcile.go: introduce cooldown window parameter and new metric labels.
- internal/slo/enforcer_test.go, internal/slo/integration_test.go: new tests that simulate concurrent events.
- deploy/helm/values.yaml: bump default cooldown to 250ms for hotfix channel.
- observability/metrics.yaml: new metric names and dashboards references.

Review conversation (summary):
- Diego Martinez (reviewer): "This change looks sensible — can we avoid a global lock?"
- Author (Avery): "We're not using a coarse global lock; the atomic compare-and-set is per-region and the cooldown is per-failover attempt. Added notes in enforcer.go comments to clarify. Also added a micro-benchmark to ensure no regressions."
- Priya Rao (reviewer): "Please add a unit test that covers a fast toggling case and assert no failover is triggered twice."
- Author: "Added integration test toggling region health at 50ms intervals; test asserts single failover and stable final state."
- Samir Patel (approver): "Approved after tests and CI green. Consider follow-up to make cooldown configurable per-customer."

CI and test summary:
- Unit tests: pass (new tests included).
- Integration tests: pass in CI cluster-1 (simulates multi-region).
- E2E smoke: pass.
- Lint/format: pass.
- Flaky tests: none flagged.

Rationale and risk assessment:
- Root cause: race between backoff evaluation and regional health reconciliation. Fix is limited to SLO enforcer state transitions and a small cooldown; does not change routing logic or persistence schema.
- Risk: low-medium. We added conservative defaults (250ms cooldown) and comprehensive tests. Observability added to monitor for regressions.

Deployment notes:
- Rolling deploy to hotfix pool first (canary 10%), monitor new metrics: slo_enforcer_failover_attempts, slo_enforcer_failover_cooldown_hits, slo_enforcer_decision_latency.
- If stable after 30 minutes, rollout to all regions.

Merge outcome: Squash and merge performed by Samir Patel after reviews approved and CI green. Hotfix was deployed to hotfix pool immediately and promoted to production within 2 hours.

Related tickets: ENG-1812 (stability investigation), ENG-1974 (follow-up: per-customer cooldown config), SUP-4321 (incident).
